$comment: Thai subtitle timing, segmentation, and style (PHASE 9). Every number here is a decision with a source, not a default that happened to look fine. Consumed by scripts/lib/subtitle.py; see DECISIONS.md ADR-033 and ADR-035.

reading.$comment: Thai is read by syllable block, not by word - a reader takes in more characters per second than in a spaced script. These figures follow the Netflix Thai timed-text style guide, which is the only widely published Thai-specific set. They are a starting point, not a measurement of this narrator's audience.
reading.source: Netflix Timed Text Style Guide - Thai; min duration 5/6s and 20cps are its adult-programme values
reading.confidence: estimate - unreviewed by a Thai speaker (outstanding since PHASE 4.2)

layout.$comment: Thai has no space between words. A cue broken at a character count can split a syllable, orphan a final consonant, or separate a combining mark from the consonant it sits on - the last of which is not merely ugly, it renders as a different string.
never_break: between a base consonant and a combining vowel or tone mark
inside a syllable produced by the PHASE 7 G2P parse
before a final consonant, separating it from its syllable

style.$comment: font_files are candidates, probed in order. Noto Sans Thai is the portable answer; Thonburi ships with macOS and is the development fallback. A font without Thai coverage must never be silently substituted - it renders as boxes.

output.$comment: ADR-035: the sidecar is the default and the reviewable artefact. Burn-in requires a shaping engine (Raqm/HarfBuzz in Pillow, or libass under ffmpeg); without one, Thai tone marks are placed by glyph advance and land beside the consonant instead of above it.
